standard.title: Interpret across a wide range of texts
standard.description: interpret information, ideas and perspectives in a wide range of spoken, written and multimodal texts and respond appropriately to cultural context, purpose and audience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can locate and process information in familiar texts and respond with some awareness of cultural context (AC9LS8EC04). They have not yet interpreted information across a wide range of text types, distinguished fact from opinion, or produced responses that demonstrate nuanced awareness of cultural context and audience.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret information, ideas and perspectives in a wide range of spoken, written and multimodal target language texts, and produce responses that are appropriate to the cultural context, purpose and audience of the original text — including texts with divergent perspectives.

nodes.label: Interpreting a wide range of text types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret information and ideas from a wider range of text types than encountered at Y7-8, including some unfamiliar formats and longer or more complex texts.
nodes.minimum_width: Successfully interpret key information from at least one text type not previously encountered (e.g. a documentary segment, a blog, a journalistic report, a personal commentary).
nodes.typical_width: Apply comprehension and interpretation strategies across a range of spoken, written and multimodal texts — including informative, persuasive and imaginative texts; travel and cultural texts; contemporary digital texts; and texts by First Nations authors or relating to First Nations contexts.
wider: Compare how the same event or topic is covered across two or more target language sources — identify differences in framing, emphasis or omission
Interpret a text from outside the target language community (e.g. a translated or shared cultural text) and consider how cultural context affects interpretation

response_modes.reason: Interpretation strategies developed through familiar text types do not automatically transfer to unfamiliar formats. Deliberate exposure to a wide range of text types — especially spoken and multimodal — builds the flexible comprehension repertoire the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Authentic text encounters across a wide range of formats are where students experience the target language as a real communicative system used for real purposes. The breadth of text encounter is itself a significant part of the intercultural and linguistic learning at Y9-10.
success_criteria: Interprets key information from at least three different target language text types in spoken, written and multimodal modes
Can identify the purpose and intended audience of an unfamiliar text type in the target language

nodes.label: Distinguishing perspective and identifying bias
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify different perspectives in target language texts and distinguish between fact and opinion.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one factual claim and one opinion or perspective in a target language text and explain the difference.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and compare different perspectives in informative and persuasive texts; distinguish fact from opinion; recognise where texts position the reader or viewer; analyse how language choices reflect and reinforce a perspective.
wider: Compare media coverage of the same issue across target language and Australian English sources — identify where perspective shapes the language choices
Investigate how language is used to position readers in a target language persuasive text — identify specific linguistic features (word choice, framing, omission) that signal perspective
nodes.hinge_reason: Distinguishing fact from opinion and identifying perspective are preconditions for the analytical and evaluative responses required in EC04 and EC05 at Y9-10. Students who treat all text content as equally factual cannot produce appropriately critical responses — and cannot engage with the divergent perspective texts the descriptor specifies.

response_modes.reason: Perspective analysis requires explicit instruction in how language encodes point of view — students need frameworks for identifying opinion markers, hedging language, framing choices and omission before they can apply these analytically to target language texts.

success_criteria: Can identify at least one factual claim and one opinion in a target language text and explain the distinction
Can identify at least one language feature in a text that signals a particular perspective

nodes.label: Responding with cultural and audience awareness
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can produce responses to target language texts that demonstrate nuanced awareness of cultural context, purpose and intended audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce one response to a target language text that addresses its cultural context, purpose and intended audience — going beyond content summary.
nodes.typical_width: Produce responses across text types (written, spoken, multimodal) that are appropriate to the cultural context and audience of the original; modify, adapt or extend texts for a different audience or purpose; respond to imaginative texts by engaging with cultural and creative elements.
wider: Adapt a target language text for a significantly different audience (e.g. produce a simplified version for a second language learner, or a version for a community unfamiliar with the cultural context) — discuss the choices made
Respond to a target language imaginative text by incorporating new cultural or creative elements — discuss how the additions relate to the original text's cultural context

response_modes.reason: Culturally aware response integrates text-type knowledge, perspective analysis and cultural understanding into a purposeful communicative act. Tasks that require students to produce responses genuinely tailored to a different audience — not just 'answer the questions' — are the key structure here.

success_criteria: Produces a response that addresses cultural context and audience — not only content
Response demonstrates awareness of the purpose of the original text and is appropriately shaped by that awareness
